title: Aperitivo & Classic Sours
description: Foundational classics known by every cocktail enthusiast and lounge bartender worldwide.
pair_1_spec: 1 oz Gin, 1 oz Campari, 1 oz Sweet Vermouth
pair_1_lore: Invented at Caffè Casoni in Florence in 1919 when Count Camillo Negroni requested gin instead of soda.

pair_2_lore: A Cuban mining town classic that serves as the ultimate test of balance between rum, lime, and sugar.

pair_8_lore: Popularized in the Royal Navy by Rear Admiral Sir Thomas Gimlette to combat scurvy among officers.

title: Highballs, Fizzes & Long Drinks
description: Refreshing effervescent highballs that celebrate lengthened spirits citrus and premium carbonation.
pair_1_spec: 2 oz Old Tom Gin, 1 oz Lemon, 1/2 oz Simple, Club Soda
pair_1_lore: Born from the Great Tom Collins Hoax of 1874 that sent New Yorkers racing to bars looking for a slanderer.

pair_2_lore: Mexico's most beloved everyday highball traditionally paired with Squirt or Jarritos grapefruit soda.
pair_2_svg: <svg viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.8"><rect x="7" y="4" width="10" height="16" rx="1"></rect><line x1="7" y1="9" x2="17" y2="9"></line><line x1="10" y1="14" x2="14" y2="14"></line></svg>

pair_3_lore: Devised in 1941 to popularize Smirnoff vodka and Cock 'n Bull ginger beer; served in distinctive copper mugs.

pair_5_spec: 1 oz Gin, 1/2 oz Lemon Juice, 1/2 oz Simple Syrup, Champagne
pair_5_lore: Named after the French 75mm field artillery gun for its remarkably punchy celebratory kick.

pair_6_spec: 1.5 oz Campari, 1.5 oz Sweet Vermouth, Splash of Soda
pair_6_lore: Originally known as the Milano-Torino; renamed due to its immense popularity with American tourists during Prohibition.
pair_6_svg: <svg viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.8"><rect x="7" y="5" width="10" height="15" rx="1"></rect><line x1="7" y1="10" x2="17" y2="10"></line></svg>
pair_7_spec: 2 oz Gin, 1 oz Lemon Juice, 3/4 oz Simple Syrup, Club Soda
pair_7_lore: A vigorously shaken classic sour topped with soda water celebrated for its tight pillowy carbonation.
pair_7_svg: <svg viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.8"><rect x="8" y="4" width="8" height="16" rx="1"></rect><circle cx="12" cy="8" r="1"></circle><circle cx="12" cy="12" r="1"></circle><circle cx="12" cy="16" r="1"></circle></svg>
pair_8_spec: 2 oz Brandy or Bourbon, Ginger Ale, 2 dashes Bitters, Long Lemon Peel
pair_8_lore: Defined by its signature uncut spiral of lemon peel draped over the rim resembling a horse's neck.
pair_8_svg: <svg viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.8"><rect x="7" y="5" width="10" height="15" rx="1"></rect><path d="M17 5c-2 3-5 5-7 8"></path></svg>

title: Botanicals, Bitters & Fortified Wine
description: Complex spirit-forward stirred masterpieces emphasizing botanical balance and aromatic fortification.
pair_1_spec: 1.5 oz Old Tom Gin, 1.5 oz Sweet Vermouth, 1/4 oz Maraschino, Angostura
pair_1_lore: The 19th-century grandfather of the modern Martini bridges heavy botanical gin and rich vermouth.
pair_1_svg: <svg viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.8"><path d="M5 4h14l-4 7H9L5 4z"></path><line x1="12" y1="11" x2="12" y2="19"></line><line x1="8" y1="19" x2="16" y2="19"></line></svg>
pair_2_spec: 2 oz Rye Whiskey, 1 Sugar Cube, 3 dashes Peychaud's, Herbsaint/Absinthe Rinse
pair_2_lore: Official cocktail of New Orleans served chilled without ice in an aromatic absinthe-rinsed glass.
pair_2_svg: <svg viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.8"><rect x="6" y="6" width="12" height="13" rx="1.5"></rect><line x1="9" y1="15" x2="15" y2="15"></line></svg>
pair_3_spec: 3/4 oz Rye, 3/4 oz Cognac, 3/4 oz Sweet Vermouth, Barspoon Bénédictine, Bitters
pair_3_lore: Crafted in 1938 by Walter Bergeron at the legendary Carousel Piano Bar in the French Quarter.

pair_4_spec: 1.25 oz Bourbon or Rye, 1 oz Campari, 1 oz Sweet Vermouth
pair_4_lore: Created by Erskine Gwynne for expatriates in 1920s Paris swapping gin for American whiskey.
pair_4_svg: <svg viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.8"><path d="M6 5h12l-3 7H9L6 5z"></path><line x1="12" y1="12" x2="12" y2="19"></line><line x1="8" y1="19" x2="16" y2="19"></line></svg>
pair_5_spec: 1.5 oz London Dry Gin, 1.5 oz Sweet Vermouth, 2 dashes Fernet-Branca
pair_5_lore: Invented by Ada Coleman at London's Savoy Hotel American Bar for theatrical actor Sir Charles Hawtrey.
pair_5_svg: <svg viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.8"><path d="M5 4h14l-4 8H9L5 4z"></path><line x1="12" y1="12" x2="12" y2="20"></line><line x1="8" y1="20" x2="16" y2="20"></line></svg>
pair_6_spec: 1 oz Gin, 1 oz Green Chartreuse, 1 oz Sweet Vermouth, Dash Orange Bitters
pair_6_lore: Named after jewels: diamond (gin) emerald (Chartreuse) and ruby (sweet vermouth).
pair_7_spec: 1.5 oz Fino Sherry, 1.5 oz Dry Vermouth, 2 dashes Angostura & Orange Bitters
pair_7_lore: Created in the 1890s by German bartender Louis Eppinger at the Grand Hotel in Yokohama Japan.
pair_7_svg: <svg viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.8"><path d="M7 5h10l-2 7a3 3 0 0 1-6 0L7 5z"></path><line x1="12" y1="12" x2="12" y2="19"></line><line x1="9" y1="19" x2="15" y2="19"></line></svg>

pair_8_lore: Originated at Philadelphia's Bellevue-Stratford Hotel in the 1880s for prominent literary club members.

description: Multi-rum harmonies exotic spice syrups orgeat and mid-century tropical escapism.

pair_1_lore: Conceived by Victor 'Trader Vic' Bergeron; when served to Tahitian friends Carrie and Eastham Guild they cried 'Mai Tai-Roa Aé!'.

pair_5_lore: Martinique & Guadeloupe's national emblem served according to 'chacun prépare sa propre mort' (each prepares their own death).

description: Equal-parts puzzles obscure revivers and historical concoctions of the Golden and Speakeasy Eras.

pair_8_lore: Cuban Prohibition-era icon crafted at the Sevilla Biltmore Hotel in Havana for President Mario García Menocal.
